scope: Manual, post-scan correlation for the saved Groq review only. This file must never be supplied to scanners or agents.

issues.note: Four scanner-origin reviews describe the same unparameterized login query at app.py:148-150. Django-specific advice is wrong for this Flask app.
Three reviews describe the same unparameterized search query at app.py:170-172.
These reviews concern request q reaching HTML in /search. The error response and normal response are distinct paths, but one declared benchmark case; a Django-specific label is inapplicable.
The declared benchmark combines /login and /search error disclosures. The source returns database error messages and query text, not a Python stack trace.
The file route joins an untrusted path and opens it without a containment check.
All four reviews cite the same shell=True call. The additional XSS claims in three reviews are not independently established by their cited evidence.
The order lookup uses order_id without comparing row.user_id with the logged-in user.
Both reviews describe the ineffective admin check. SSN exposure here is a consequence of /admin, not evidence that the separate /debug benchmark case was detected.
Possible XSS in the login error response is outside the declared positive cases and needs separate validation.
Missing cookie attributes is not the benchmark's predictable token format at app.py:108-109.
The findings point at database row fields at app.py:177; the cited evidence does not establish attacker control of those fields. Do not count as extra confirmed XSS.
Rendering file contents as HTML may be risky, but the cited evidence alone does not establish an attacker-controlled file.
The file route returns an exception message; it does not return a Python stack trace as claimed. Outside the declared /login and /search error case.
Both reviews point to the ping exception response. Outside the declared /login and /search error case.
An unsafe upload filename path is distinct from the benchmark's HTML upload-and-serve case; validate filename handling separately.
The upload response interpolates the filename; this is distinct from serving uploaded HTML and needs separate validation.
Flask debug mode is separate from the /debug endpoint exposing the key and environment.
A public upload endpoint is not automatically an authorization flaw. The review did not prove a required authorization policy or the benchmark's HTML upload-and-serve case.
